content:
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model underestimates during sharp downward trends, particularly when true values dip below 70.
- Overshoots after recent spikes (e.g., 75+), then fails to correct downward — model holds high values too long.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model lags behind true mean (~71.5–72.5) and takes 3–5 days to adjust.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than true price volatility — underestimates short-term volatility spikes.
- When true price drops below 70, model often fails to recognize it as a “new low” and continues to forecast higher.
- Model exhibits “memory bias” — overweights recent high values (last 5–7 days) and underweights true trend reversals.
- Forecast horizon 30d is too long for short-term mean reversion — model should adjust to 10–15d horizon for accuracy.
